acts.act_one: Opens in medias res with a dual-mystery hook: Grace awakens in a spacecraft medical bay with retrograde amnesia alongside two mummified crewmates and discovers he is in another solar system (Tau Ceti) with forty days of fuel left. Intercuts this survival crisis with a chronological Earth flashback track that establishes the global inciting incident: the discovery of the 'Petrova Line'—an alien single-celled organism ('Astrophage') draining the sun's luminance and threatening human extinction within thirty years. In the past, UN taskforce head Eva Stratt drafts Grace out of his sixth-grade classroom to isolate the organism's infrared propulsion and reproduction; in the present, after a drunken meltdown and jettisoning his dead crewmates, Grace decelerates into the Tau Ceti system and encounters a massive alien vessel.
acts.act_two: Driven by a cross-species scientific buddy-alliance in the present braided with escalating pre-launch preparations in the past. Through exterior thruster-flares, tethered canisters, and an umbilical tunnel, Grace makes first contact with 'Rocky,' a blind, five-legged, ammonia-breathing Eridian engineer whose twenty-two crewmates died of radiation sickness. Using raised-numeral clocks and a laptop Fourier-transform waveform analyzer, they build a shared vocabulary, move Rocky aboard the Hail Mary, and deduce that planet 'Adrian' (Tau Ceti E) harbors a natural Astrophage predator; at the midpoint, Rocky reveals he has enough excess fuel to send Grace back to Earth alive. Simultaneously, Earth flashbacks reveal the ninety-one-day isolation psychosis problem, the 1-in-7,000 coma-resistance gene requirement, and Grace training the prime astronauts (Yao, Ilyukhina, Dubois). The act culminates in a double catastrophe: a lab explosion in Russia kills Dubois and Shapiro nine days before launch, match-cutting to Grace and Rocky's harrowing 10-kilometer chain-fishing maneuver in Adrian's atmosphere, where a fuel-tank breach nearly crushes them under centrifugal force until Rocky breaches his own ammonia habitat into Earth air—fatally scorching himself—to save Grace.
acts.act_three: Opens with the penultimate flashback revealing Stratt's ruthless pragmatism: with Dubois dead and no time to train a replacement, she demands Grace take the suicide mission. In the present, a recovering Grace and Rocky isolate the predator ('Taumoeba'), breed a nitrogen-resistant strain (82.5), celebrate with a bathysphere tour of Rocky's ship, and part ways toward their respective homeworlds—intercut with the final flashback twist where Grace refuses the mission as a 'coward' and is forcibly sedated and dragged onto the ship by Stratt's guards. On his way back to Earth, Grace discovers that Taumoeba 82.5 evolved to permeate solid-state xenonite, meaning Rocky's xenonite ship is stranded with dead fuel lines. Facing a binary choice between his own survival and his friend's, Grace redeems his past cowardice: he launches four unmanned 'Beetle' probes to save Earth and turns the Hail Mary around to rescue Rocky. Closes with a dual epilogue: Stratt watching Grace's farewell log as Earth launches its recovery rocket, and a 'Sixteen Years Later' coda on Erid where an elderly Grace learns Earth's sun has returned to full luminance before teaching physics to a classroom of thirty Eridian children.

mystery_hiding: Constructed on a bifurcated temporal architecture where the protagonist's clinical coma-amnesia serves as a natural gating mechanism for audience information. The script withholds two parallel sets of mysteries: in the space timeline, why Tau Ceti is immune to Astrophage and how to communicate with and survive alongside an alien biology; in the Earth timeline, how a disgraced sixth-grade teacher ended up as the sole surviving astronaut on humanity's last-hope starship. The script deliberately plants a false assumption of heroism throughout Acts One and Two—allowing both the audience and Rocky ('You are brave human') to assume Grace volunteered after the explosion killed Dubois—before engineering the devastating late-Act-Two/early-Act-Three flashback reveal in Stratt's office and the medical ward: Grace actually begged for his life, admitted he was a coward, and was drugged and forced onto the ship against his will, which directly sets up his voluntary self-sacrifice to save Rocky in the climax.
character_connections: Built around a triangular thematic contrast between Grace, Eva Stratt, and Rocky. In the past timeline, Stratt operates as an immovable, utilitarian authoritarian ('There is greater purpose to life beyond the self') who strips away Grace's comfortable, risk-averse detachment—forcing him from a classroom bystander into an unwilling martyr. In the present timeline, Rocky functions as Grace's evolutionary and emotional mirror: both are the sole survivors of their respective crews, and their skills interlock symmetrically (Grace provides theoretical molecular biology, radiation physics, and computer software; Rocky provides miraculous mechanical engineering, xenonite metallurgy, and extra fuel). Their bond progresses through physical barriers—from external ship thrusters, to a divided hexagon tunnel, to watching each other sleep, to Rocky entering Earth air to save Grace, and Grace entering a bathysphere to visit Rocky's ship—transforming Grace from the coward who betrayed Stratt's faith into the hero who sacrifices his return ticket to Earth for Rocky.
spine: A risk-averse former scientist who was forced onto a one-way interstellar mission against his will overcomes his cowardice through a profound friendship with an alien survivor, ultimately choosing to sacrifice his chance to return home in order to save his friend and his species.
key_structural_decisions: Amnesia-driven dual-timeline braiding: intercutting the chronological pre-launch Earth narrative with the present-day Tau Ceti mission so that each recovered memory directly informs or ironizes the immediate scientific crisis in space.

The late-stage moral inversion twist: withholding the final two Earth flashbacks (Stratt's office and the forced sedation) until the exact moment Grace and Rocky part ways as 'brave' heroes, retroactively reframing Grace's entire presence in space as involuntary conscription right before he must make a voluntary choice to turn back.

Progressive communication scaffolding with Rocky: structuring the second act around an escalating ladder of translation mechanics—from thruster flares, to 3D models in canisters, to proton-bead necklaces, to tactile clocks, to a laptop waveform lookup table, to a live text-to-speech ship interface, and finally to subtitled fluency in the epilogue.

Diegetic video-log framing ('camera box'): using Grace's onboard documentation camera and the dormitory's 'Don't Go Crazy Wall' viewscreen to externalize solitary scientific exposition in Act One, which later pays off structurally as the exact recording Stratt watches on the returned Beetle probe in Act Three.

Circular classroom bookending: opening Grace's pre-mission identity at a whiteboard teaching sixth graders on Earth about the dying sun, and ending the entire film sixteen years later with Grace at the front of a domed classroom on Erid teaching thirty Eridian children the speed of light.
scene_rhythm: Alternates between methodical, procedural 'competence-porn' problem-solving sequences (microscope diagnostics, whiteboard math calculations, language-building montages) and high-velocity, physics-driven action set-pieces (zero-g tumbles, the 10-kilometer reverse-thrust atmospheric chain drop, the centrifugal fuel-tank breach, the emergency vacuum-venting). Cross-cutting between the claustrophobic, two-character intimacy of the spacecraft and the expansive, multi-character bureaucratic tension of the Earth flashbacks keeps the pacing propulsive, using sharp match-cuts and pre-laps (such as the Russian launchpad explosion cutting directly to the Adrian orbital dive) to bridge timelines.
